messages.author: bff9e4feca8b059f
messages.subject: Shiny and Select2 interaction during page load
parts:
I have a rather intricate select2 setup that involves a handful of ajax calls to transform some initial URL GET parameters into Shiny input-bound identifiers, but for this to work select2 needs to fiddle with input values; which of course Shiny sniffs and sends invalid input to the server.  I'd like to "defer" Shiny's input bindings until after select2 is all finished, though select2's work involves multiple async ajax calls.  I tried Shiny.unbindAll() before my select2 code, but got Uncaught TypeError: Object #<Object> has no method 'unbindAll'. (presumably since initShiny() had not yet been called) I guess I could use an .ajaxStop() handler to call Shiny.bindAll(), but is there a way to call initShiny() directly (when my select2 stuff is all done), not by timeout?

Thanks,
-Aaron

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny and Select2 interaction during page load
parts:
John, grey-outs from long server processing is a feature, not a bug--it shows the user what output(s) are being recalculated. If you don't like it you can override the CSS to have a different, or no, effect. This is what the original CSS rule looks like:
.recalculating {
  opacity: 0.3;
  transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
  -moz-transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
  -webkit-transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
  -o-transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
}
You can apply your own styles for .recalculating to change the opacity to 1 and then do other stuff instead.

The app never crashes on local, so I assume the websocket connection to the server is closing.  Is there a hacky way to ensure the connection stays alive?  Like could I do a calculation every 30 seconds make sure R stays awake?

John



On Thursday, May 30, 2013 12:53:51 PM UTC-4, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
That usually means the app has crashed, or the websocket connection to the server has closed for another reason. If that happens, bring up your browser's JavaScript console, it may contain clues, including the R process's stderr output if available.


On Thu, May 30, 2013 at 6:00 AM, John Luis <jta...@gmail.com> wrote:
Sorry, I'm not talking about that grey-out.  I actually like that feature very much.  I'm talking about the whole screen going grey.  I could click through tabs and see things but can't execute things anymore.  Usually happens within 5 minutes of inactivity.  I have to refresh the window but then the app has to re-run again completely.

Thanks,
John



On Wednesday, May 29, 2013 7:02:00 PM UTC-4, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
John, grey-outs from long server processing is a feature, not a bug--it shows the user what output(s) are being recalculated. If you don't like it you can override the CSS to have a different, or no, effect. This is what the original CSS rule looks like:
.recalculating {
  opacity: 0.3;
  transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
  -moz-transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
  -webkit-transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
  -o-transition: opacity 250ms ease 500ms;
}
You can apply your own styles for .recalculating to change the opacity to 1 and then do other stuff instead.

I get constant grey-outs too (on server, not on local) and want to try this trick you mentioned.  How do I implement this?  I'm confused by the comment in the // line.

On Monday, February 18, 2013 2:44:58 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
There are no such callbacks today unfortunately, but you might be able to get away with this:

$(function() {
  setTimeout(function() {
    Shiny.unbindAll();
    // Do your work and then call Shiny.bindAll()
  }, 10);
});



On Mon, Feb 18, 2013 at 6:59 AM, Aaron Mackey <ajma...@gmail.com> wrote:
I'm still struggling with this; is there a way for me to "interrupt" the initShiny() callback before the timeout occurs, so that I can make sure other processing has finished before I then let initShiny do its work?  Or alternatively, can I get initShiny to then immediately call my own function (where I could then unbind/bindAll safely)?

Thanks for any help,
-Aaron

On Tuesday, February 12, 2013 12:43:20 PM UTC-5, Aaron Mackey wrote:
I have a rather intricate select2 setup that involves a handful of ajax calls to transform some initial URL GET parameters into Shiny input-bound identifiers, but for this to work select2 needs to fiddle with input values; which of course Shiny sniffs and sends invalid input to the server.  I'd like to "defer" Shiny's input bindings until after select2 is all finished, though select2's work involves multiple async ajax calls.  I tried Shiny.unbindAll() before my select2 code, but got Uncaught TypeError: Object #<Object> has no method 'unbindAll'. (presumably since initShiny() had not yet been called) I guess I could use an .ajaxStop() handler to call Shiny.bindAll(), but is there a way to call initShiny() directly (when my select2 stuff is all done), not by timeout?

Thanks,
-Aaron

The apps on glimmer don't crash for me after inactivity.  On my own apps' JS console, I've always had the error below.  I never minded it since it always ran perfectly on local.  But no such luck on server.  I wonder if this could be tied to the grey-out...

  1. Port error: Could not establish connection. Receiving end does not exist. miscellaneous_bindings:235
    1. chromeHidden.Port.dispatchOnDisconnect
